sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: The tea plant is an evergreen shrub or small tree that can reach about 17 m if left unpruned; plantations commonly keep it below 2 m for harvesting. Its toothed leaves are picked for tea, and seeds can be pressed for oil. The flowers have pale petals and many stamens; the fruit is a capsule with brown seeds.

sections.title: Food and image
sections.text: Tea leaves are processed to make black, green and other teas; they contain caffeine and excessive consumption can cause adverse effects. The plate's toothed leaves, white flower, numerous stamens and seed capsule match the species. Petal counts vary among descriptions.
